tip: Perfective verbs make the future in one word, no будем (budem) needed: купим (kupim) already means we will buy.
For weather and existence, будет (budet) alone means there will be: будет дождь (budet dozhd = there will be rain).
The verb быть (byt = to be) builds the future: буду (budu = I will) plus an imperfective infinitive like ждать (zhdat = to wait).
Most masculine past verbs end in the -l sound, but помог (pomog = he helped) drops it entirely.
The past ending reveals the speaker's gender: написала (napisala) ending in -la means a woman is speaking.
The verb найти (nayti = to find) has an irregular past: нашёл (nashyol = found), where the stem changes completely.
For a repeated past action use the imperfective: покупал (pokupal = kept buying) fits каждый день (kazhdyy den = every day).
The imperfective past also means used to: открывал (otkryval = used to open) matches the habit каждое утро (kazhdoye utro = every morning).
читал (chital = was reading) marks the activity with no result, while perfective дочитал (dochital = finished reading) marks completion.
Duration words like долго (dolgo = for a long time) pair with the imperfective: помогали (pomogali = were helping), never the perfective.
писать (pisat = to write) shifts to пишет (pishet = writes) in the present, with the s sound becoming sh.
The verb помогать (pomogat = to help) takes the dative, so mom becomes маме (mame), not маму (mamu).
In the morning is just the instrumental used as a time word: Утром (utrom), from утро (utro = morning).
The word с (s = with) takes the instrumental case, turning we into с нами (s nami = with us).
нужно (nuzhno = need) puts the person in the dative: Ей нужно (yey nuzhno = she needs), literally to her it is needed.
A container plus its contents puts the contents in the genitive: воды (vody = of water), from вода (voda = water).
A few masculine nouns take a stressed -u in the location form: в саду (v sadu = in the garden), not в саде (v sade).
The word перед (pered = before) takes the instrumental: перед завтраком (pered zavtrakom = before breakfast).
By bus is на (na) plus the prepositional case: на автобусе (na avtobuse), the standard way to name transport.
The word нет (net = there is no) forces the genitive: молоко (moloko = milk) becomes нет молока (net moloka = no milk).
For repeated days use по (po) plus the dative plural: по пятницам (po pyatnitsam = on Fridays), from пятница (pyatnitsa = Friday).
After 2, 3, 4 the noun is genitive singular: три килограмма (tri kilogramma = three kilograms), not килограммы (kilogrammy).
Animate masculine nouns use their genitive form as the object: сантехника (santekhnika = plumber), governed by вызвать (vyzvat = to call).
интереснее (interesneye = more interesting) is the comparative, and чем (chem = than) introduces what it is compared against.
